neighbours.label: 'during' / 'after' (and similar) in the time course of a disease or exposure
fire: A rash usually appears three to five days after infection with the virus.
Symptoms may worsen during the first weeks of chemotherapy.
Most joint damage occurs during the early stage of the disease.
Swelling around the wound can develop within hours after the bite.
Fever and chills often begin two days after exposure to the bacteria.
Patients lose weight rapidly during the acute phase of the illness.
Hair loss is common in the months after treatment begins.
The child developed a cough a week after the first symptoms of measles.
quiet: A parade usually takes place three to five days after the harvest festival.
Traffic may worsen during the first weeks of the school year.
Most of the shouting occurs during the final minutes of the match.
Guests can check in within hours after the ferry arrives.
Prices often rise two days after the announcement of the budget.
Students study hard during the busy weeks before the exams.
Sales are slow in the months after the holidays end.
The child started reading a week after the first day of school.

notes: Card: ' during' x5, ' after' x4, e.g. 'affected during the first 6 months of active disease', 'carbuncles within 10 days after first contact', 'one to six days after the bite'. The + pole fires on the same words in everyday narrative ('a diner after', 'minutes after the meeting'), so near misses use these words outside medicine.
